stories.headline: Source: Packers signing veteran O-lineman Mekhi Becton
stories.summary: Veteran offensive lineman Mekhi Becton is signing with the Packers, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.
stories.body:
Veteran offensive lineman Mekhi Becton is signing with the Green Bay Packers, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.

Becton becomes the second veteran addition to the Packers' offensive line, joining guard Laken Tomlinson, who the Packers signed off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad.

The Packers have struggled to produce a running game and to protect quarterback Jordan Love due to injuries on the offensive line. Guard Aaron Banks has missed two of the first three games due to injuries and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending torn patellar tendon in Week 2.

Becton was a free agent after the Los Angeles Chargers released him in the offseason, one year after signing him to a two-year, $20 million contract in 2025.

The six-year veteran battled injuries throughout the 2025 season and voiced his frustration with the Chargers at one point last November.

The 6-foot-7, 363-pound Becton appeared in 15 games -- 14 starts -- last season with the Chargers. However, he ranked as the 49th-worst guard in pass block win rate (91.2%) and the third-worst lineman (127th) in run block win rate (63.4%).

Becton, 27, played just 72% of snaps in 2025 and played 100% of snaps in only six games. He missed two games, one with a concussion and another because of a knee injury. (Becton sat out the Chargers' final regular-season game with other starters.) He was also regularly rotated in games; a move the team said was to protect him from injury.

A first-round draft selection of the Jets in 2020, he struggled through four injury-plagued seasons playing offensive tackle in New York before enjoying a revival in 2024 with the Super Bowl champion Philadelphia Eagles, who moved him to guard.

ESPN's Kris Rhim contributed to this report.

stories.headline: NBA regular-season buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
stories.summary: Here are the deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including intel from Monday's media days.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Tuesday as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association will join them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams Tuesday.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 28

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey friendship, helping Embiid were 76ers factors
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Reeve named WNBA Coach of Year after leading Lynx to best record
stories.summary: Cheryl Reeve was named WNBA Coach of the Year for the fifth time, extending her own league record, after guiding the Minnesota Lynx to a 33-11 record and the No. 1 seed in the playoffs.
stories.body:
Cheryl Reeve was named WNBA Coach of the Year for the fifth time, extending her own league record, after guiding the Minnesota Lynx to a 33-11 record and the No. 1 seed in the playoffs.

Reeve, in her 17th season as Minnesota's coach, beat out the Golden State Valkyries' Natalie Nakase and Washington Mystics' Sydney Johnson for the award announced Monday.

The Lynx finished a game ahead of the 32-12 Valkyries despite losing star forward Napheesa Collier for the first half of the season as she recovered from offseason surgery on both ankles.

Reeve, who is also president of basketball operations for the club, previously won the award in 2011, 2016, 2020 and 2024. She guided the Lynx to WNBA titles in 2011, 2013, 2015 and 2017.

Reeve received 40 of 74 votes from media panel. Nakase, who won the award last year, finished second with 20 votes. Johnson was third with 14 votes.

stories.headline: MLB playoffs 2026: Could Dodgers be more vulnerable than you think?
stories.summary: A three-peat might feel inevitable, but there are no guarantees for this L.A. squad. Here's why.
stories.body:
To the Los Angeles Dodgers, the bye used to be an obstacle. In 2022 and 2023, they won enough games to skip the wild-card round, only to be on their heels against inferior division series opponents who easily dispatched them. The break, in their minds, helped trigger an early exit. And yet, it remains the overwhelming preference.

They don't want their season distilled to a best-of-three series, which amounts to a coin flip.

Besides, they could use the rest.

"There's a lot of us kind of limping toward the end here," Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman said. "A lot of aches and pains this year."

Freeman is at the center of a Dodgers position-player group that is the oldest in the sport -- one that has also played a lot more baseball than any other over these past 40 or so months. The Dodgers conquered the bye on their way to a championship in 2024 and experienced the toll of having to overcome four playoff rounds en route to last year's title.

Now, as they look to become the first National League team to three-peat, they'll watch as the Atlanta Braves and the Philadelphia Phillies fight for the right to play them in the NL Division Series, which begins Saturday.

The Dodgers lost each of their past five series against playoff teams this season, going a combined 2-14 against the Braves, San Diego Padres, Milwaukee Brewers, Chicago Cubs and Boston Red Sox. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts dismissed those struggles recently.

"I don't put any stock into it," he said. "Once you get to the postseason, it's a different season."

The Dodgers believe their toughest battles are waged internally. If their pitchers are healthy, if their hitters are on track, if their roles are defined, they consider themselves superior. But this season has tested that. A $380 million payroll did not rid them of concerns, many of which they'll carry into October.

Below, we explore the ways the two-time defending champions might be vulnerable this postseason.

The offense has been inconsistent all season. Will it produce in October?

Internally, the offense represents the Dodgers' biggest concern going into the playoffs, a time of year when runs are exceedingly difficult to manufacture.

This, more than anywhere else, is where age could be a factor. Their .214/.317/.376 slash line with runners in scoring position in September was cause for alarm. And so was Freeman, who batted .184 and produced only one extra-base hit all month while continuing to bat second, third or fourth.

The Dodgers' offense was especially bad in July and August, putting up a .699 OPS that ranked 22nd among the 30 teams.

Some signs of life have emerged recently. Teoscar Hernández opened his stance, got healthier and started pulverizing the baseball. Mookie Betts found his rhythm and began to produce the way he did in the early 2020s. Kyle Tucker reworked his pregame routine with the Dodgers' hitting coaches, found a way to slot his swing more consistently and went on a nice run, ending a miserable first season in L.A. on a positive note.

Add Will Smith looking more like his All-Star self, Andy Pages making it back from a hand fracture with little incident, and Shohei Ohtani returning from the injured list -- more on him shortly -- and you have the makings of a group capable of meeting its lofty expectations.

But that doesn't mean the Dodgers' offense is humming.

Maybe Freeman fixes himself during the bye, not unlike how he found something in the days between the NL Championship Series and World Series in 2024. Maybe Tucker's recent run is a sign he's finally back, not a mirage like the one the Dodgers experienced from their $60 million-a-year outfielder in July. Maybe this version of Betts and Hernández changes the dynamic entirely. But there's uncertainty here.

For an aging lineup that has played a lot of baseball over these past three years, the bye could be a godsend. Or, like in 2022 and 2023, it could be a death knell for an offense seeking momentum.

Ohtani has been hurt and won't pitch in the playoffs. Is he healthy enough?

The Dodgers were initially encouraged by how Ohtani was swinging and moving upon returning to the lineup in the middle of last week, but as the days went on and the production lagged, concern resurfaced.

Ohtani went 5-for-21 with eight strikeouts and only one walk over the last five regular-season games. There were positives within that stretch -- nine batted balls of at least 98 mph, two flyouts to the center-field warning track, an opposite-field double off a 103 mph Mason Miller fastball -- but also plenty of negatives, especially during the weekend series at Oracle Park.

If he's rusty, this five-day layoff certainly won't help. If he's still compromised, it'll only get harder once high-pressure games get stacked atop one another. Roberts said he doesn't believe it's the latter, instead pinning Ohtani's struggles to the anxiousness of someone who knew he had few opportunities to get his timing right. In September, Ohtani played in only eight games.

"When you haven't played a lot," Roberts told reporters in San Francisco on Saturday, "there's something in you that wants to swing the bat, that wants to get hits, and knowing you don't have a lot of time left in the season."

Three weeks ago, there was no bigger concern on the Dodgers than Ohtani. He had already been ruled out of pitching, had accumulated seven hits and 22 strikeouts in his previous 54 at-bats, and the ailments that had affected him on the mound -- the sore left knee, the tight right biceps -- had seemingly migrated to the batter's box.

On Sept. 9, when the Dodgers finally decided to put Ohtani on the IL, there was no telling what to expect the rest of the way. There still isn't. Ohtani will continue to hit at the top of the Dodgers' lineup -- first against right-handers, perhaps second against left-handers -- but his ability to produce remains an open question.

The Dodgers' two-way star acknowledged previously that he won't feel totally healthy until the offseason, for obvious reasons.

"The best mode of recovery," he said, "is to completely not play."

That is no longer an option. At no point during the postseason will Ohtani be 100% healthy.

"I don't think anyone is going to be at 100% in October," Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman countered. "It's a long, grueling season, and everyone's on fumes. Our group, the teams we're playing against, everyone is on fumes. And it's so adrenaline-based that, for me, it's about each guy just drawing from their experience and having calmness in what they do. And I would bet on our talent to shine through."

The rotation has been banged up. Can it be dominant?

Tyler Glasnow gave up eight runs in 10 innings in two starts on Sept. 5 and 12. Four days later, Blake Snell exited after one inning because of tightness in his groin. Roki Sasaki was on the injured list then, Ohtani had already been ruled out of pitching, and Justin Wrobleski was navigating a rough stretch, no longer resembling the All-Star from the first half. Suddenly there was major concern about the back half of the Dodgers' postseason rotation.

That is less so the case now. Glasnow had a much more encouraging start against the Giants on Sept. 18 and looked even sharper in the early portion of his outing against the Padres on Thursday night, taking a no-hitter into the sixth inning before running into some trouble. Glasnow recorded only one out in that frame but finished with 11 strikeouts.

"Overall," he said afterward, "I feel like I'm in a pretty good rhythm right now, so it's the perfect time to be in the postseason."

Snell felt that way two weeks ago. Now, perhaps, not so much. The 33-year-old left-hander made one start over the season's first 20 weeks, came back from shoulder and elbow ailments to put up a 1.04 ERA over a six-start stretch, then tweaked his left groin on Sept. 16 and asked out. The Dodgers saw it as a proactive, precautionary move. That Snell threw two bullpen sessions, then agreed to make one final regular-season start Saturday was seen as a good sign. His performance -- four innings, one run, three strikeouts and a shoddy changeup -- wasn't great, but he came out of it healthy..

Glasnow and Snell have combined for only 51 regular-season starts over the past two years. Some of that is by design. The Dodgers are prone to giving their starting pitchers extra time to recover from injuries so that they're fresh for the stretch run. Last year, it paid off. Snell and Glasnow joined Ohtani and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in a rotation that absorbed nearly 70% of the Dodgers' postseason innings and put up a 2.55 ERA in the process.

Ohtani won't be part of this year's group, but Tarik Skubal, winner of each of the last two American League Cy Young Awards, will be. Yamamoto, meanwhile, looks just as brilliant as he did in 2025. If Glasnow and Snell are right, the Dodgers will again roll out one of the most dominant rotations in baseball history.

If not, the equation changes entirely.

The back end of the bullpen has been a problem. Can they trust it?

After being rocked for five runs in the thin air of Oklahoma City during a rehab appearance on Sept. 13, Edwin Díaz reached out to an old friend. His first season in L.A. had been a disaster, mired by elbow surgery and an 11.85 ERA. Now, he couldn't even get minor league hitters out. If not for a massive turnaround, he probably wouldn't even crack the Dodgers' postseason roster.

So Díaz called Héctor Mercado, a former big leaguer and one of his longtime pitching coaches in Puerto Rico, who suggested a mental cue to help him stay centered with his delivery. He tried it out in a bullpen session on Sept. 15 and felt good. He pitched in a minor league game again the next day and felt even better. Then he rejoined the Dodgers, and with each game, it seemed, Díaz got closer to resembling his best self.

He faced 17 batters to finish the regular season and struck out nine of them, allowing only two to reach base. But all of those appearances came in low leverage. The Dodgers won't find out how Díaz fares in a tight, pressure-filled spot until it matters most.

"I'm ready to pitch every day," Díaz said. "I just want them to keep trusting me and keep giving me the ball to show them I'm ready to pitch in the postseason."

The Dodgers don't intend to go into the playoffs with a set closer. At least not unless Díaz earns their trust again. Instead, they'll rely on a bevy of arms to hold leads, hoping that enough of them step up so that Roberts has the freedom to utilize Tanner Scott when situations call for it earlier in games. Over these past few weeks, the Dodgers have expressed confidence in the group beyond him.

They've pointed to Evan Phillips, who has looked increasingly sharp since his midseason return from Tommy John surgery; Edgardo Henriquez, who the team believes has fully recovered from a back injury; Brock Stewart, who has emerged as a trusted reliever; Alex Vesia, who significantly improved his walk rate this month; and Sasaki, who is in a much better place than he was upon being thrust into the closer's role at this time a year ago.

But it's hard to dismiss the fact that the Dodgers spent $69 million over the offseason to ensure the ninth inning was solidified, and it isn't. Roberts was asked last week if he would prefer to have a set closer in October.

"In a perfect world," he said. "As we all know, the world's not perfect."

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey team previews: Outlooks, player picks for every team
stories.summary: Get ready for the NHL regular season with outlooks and fantasy hockey picks for all 32 teams.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NHL season is nearly upon us and that brings an exciting new season of ESPN Fantasy hockey drafts, leagues and all the lineup decisions that come with them. There is fantasy value to be had on each of the NHL's 32 squads, from the obvious superstars to budding talents. It's never too late to catch up on an offseason's worth of information before your draft with a cheat sheet or draft guide, but it's the right time to take a closer look at who to look at who to draft from every team.

The NHL season starts on Tuesday, Sept. 29, but new fantasy hockey leagues start every Monday. To see how every team's strengths and weaknesses stack up before the season, check out the NHL season preview.

ESPN Fantasy analysts Sean Allen and Victoria Matiash give you a look at each team's core fantasy player picks and sleepers, with Sean writing about the Eastern Conference, and Victoria the Western Conference.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Anaheim Ducks

Cutter Gauthier -- who's ready to flirt with the 50-goal mark -- Leo Carlsson, and Beckett Sennecke are the Ducks' top fantasy forwards, in order. After that there's a considerable drop off, at least before the regular season gets underway. As Anaheim's top defenseman, Jackson LaCombe could average 2.0 fantasy points per game in ESPN Fantasy leagues. In net, Lukas Dostal is a risky play behind Anaheim's refurbished, and largely inexperienced, defense.

Boston Bruins
David Pastrnak carries this offense almost alone, and he makes linemates: Morgan Geekie and Pavel Zacha last year, maybe JJ Peterka next. Zacha's the value nobody drafts -- a center going late in drafts despite finishing a top-80 fantasy forward.

Buffalo Sabres
Two true stars up top, and a deep, ascending forward group behind Tage Thompson and Rasmus Dahlin. Jack Quinn, Josh Doan and Zach Benson all flashed, and Jiri Kulich has a chance to, and they all sit available at the end of drafts. Bet on the wave, with Doan the best of them.

Calgary Flames

A key piece of the Flames' future, Zayne Parekh is in position to make significant fantasy noise right now in anchoring the top power play. A must-roster in dynasty competition, the 20-year-old defenseman is also worth targeting in deeper redraft leagues. Tending the net for a rebuilding team, Wolf is a riskier pick in leagues that deal in negative integers for goalies. Matvei Gridin sports sneaky 65-point fantasy potential as a winger on the top line and power play.

Carolina Hurricanes
Carolina's relentless system floats everyone's floor, with Sebastian Aho, Andrei Svechnikov and Nikolaj Ehlers as the weapons. A healthy Shayne Gostisbehere is the power-play bet, as he was 22nd in assists per minute in just 55 games, so the helpers spike if he stays on the ice.

Chicago Blackhawks

Patrick Kane and Roman Kantserov (fresh from the KHL) are set to pile up points in flanking Connor Bedard at even-strength and with the extra skater, once the star center returns from injury. No one will be shocked to see the Kane hit the 70-mark in his return to Chicago. Anton Frondell is expected to break-out as the second-line center after scoring nine points in 12 games this past spring. Top dog on Chicago's blue line, Bowen Byram could rank as a top-20 defenseman once all is said and done.

Colorado Avalanche

Martin Necas accumulated 100 points riding shotgun to Nathan MacKinnon in 2025-26. No reason to expect any different this round. Lower down the fantasy ranks, Gabriel Landeskog sports greater potential, now that the captain feels good and up to speed. Especially in competing on a No. 1 power play with MacKinnon, Necas, and Cale Makar. Between the pipes, Scott Wedgewood should see fewer starts now that Mackenzie Blackwood is back to full health.

Columbus Blue Jackets
Zach Werenski's a set-and-forget anchor and Adam Fantili is ready to pop in his age-22 season. Valeri Nichushkin's the bounce-back dart -- a proven scorer whose value cratered on availability, not ability -- while Jet Greaves owns a crease that's worth your attention if Columbus banks him wins.

Dallas Stars

Even though there's some debate about whether Jason Robertson or Wyatt Johnston will eventually emerge as the Stars' ultimate fantasy performer by April, truth is that both project as top-12 forwards. Slipping through the fantasy cracks a bit, Miro Heiskanen remains a top-10 defenseman with such a solid group of dynamite skaters. If healthy, Oettinger is going to play, and win, enough to merit rostering as a No. 1 goalie.

Detroit Red Wings
Moritz Seider anchors an elite peripheral profile, but the forward core carries questions after Patrick Kane's departure and Dylan Larkin's ugly offseason. Fade Alex DeBrincat: he was fourth in the league in shots per minute last season, but that chemistry with Kane is off the table now.

Edmonton Oilers

Beyond the club's pair of bona fide superstars, Zach Hyman forecasts to bounce back after two mediocre/injury-riddled seasons. The veteran winger likes playing for Mike Babcock and seems fully fit after missing 24 games this past campaign. Evan Bouchard could eventually eclipse all fantasy blueliners if he ends up hitting the 100-point mark, as some optimistically anticipate. But managers best steer clear of Edmonton's goaltending until a clearer picture -- and a positive one -- develops.

Florida Panthers
A down fantasy year sets up a roaring return, with both Brady and Matthew Tkachuk now up front and a healthy Aleksander Barkov back. Brad Marchand is the ageless draft pick -- fourth in the entire league in goals per minute at age 38, available at a discount because he played only 52 games.

Los Angeles Kings

One of this year's more popular breakout candidates, Brandt Clarke is expected to take another step forward after amassing eight goals and 32 assists in his sophomore season. No one should feel surprised if the 23-year-old collects 25 points on the power play alone. After Artemi Panarin and Adrian Kempe are off the board, Kevin Fiala is valuable enough to draft late and start on IR. The winger is loosely due back in early November.

Minnesota Wild

The Wild are one of the few squads with two top-20 forwards. Any manager who secures Kirill Kaprizov as a No. 1 and/or Matt Boldy as a No. 2 should count themselves fortunate. While Brock Faber won't put up as many points as Quinn Hughes, the 24-year-old blueliner provides his own value by blocking shots. Often overshadowed by the former Canuck, Faber serves as a mid-round steal. After an astounding rookie campaign, and with Filip Gustavsson hurt, Jesper Wallstedt is the No. 1 goalie in Minny, at least to start.

Montreal Canadiens
A rising young team with one of the league's most dangerous power plays. Juraj Slafkovsky is the target. The former No. 1overall pick came on strong (eighth overall in fantasy points from Dec. 1 onward) and is going a full round or two behind Nick Suzuki and Cole Caufield.

Nashville Predators

Steven Stamkos is expected to take a step back after potting 42 goals (20.4% shooting percentage) in 2025-26. Making a sparkling impression in preseason competition, Matthew Wood is worth monitoring. On the blue line, perhaps because of Nashville's underwhelming showing and recent injuries, Roman Josi isn't garnering the fantasy attention of yesterday. However, if healthy -- as he is right now -- the 2020 Norris Trophy winner remains a fringe top-10 defender.

New Jersey Devils
Health is the whole story here. A healthy Jack Hughes is a first-rounder, and the top forwards are dangerous when whole. Watch the new additions, as Anthony Mantha and Luke Evangelista are near-free late fliers who could spark real value if they stick in the top six.

New York Islanders
Rookie Matthew Schaefer is the real deal, an every-week anchor from Day 1 in top-pairing, power-play minutes. He has a real shot at being the top fantasy defenseman already, if the Islanders' underwhelming power play can find its form under coach Peter DeBoer.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

New York Rangers
Loaded with established talent at the key positions: Mika Zibanejad, Adam Fox and an elite Igor Shesterkin in net. Alexis Lafreniere is the sleeper worth a late shout, as he found another gear late once the offense reshuffled post-Panarin, finishing top-50 in fantasy points after March 1 last season.

Ottawa Senators
A young core arriving all at once, now without Brady Tkachuk. It's a wealth of talent with Tim Stutzle driving the bus. Linus Ullmark is worth a look to bounce back to his Vezina Trophy-winning form. After a lost regular season, he was not to blame for the Sens being swept in the first round (.932 save percentage).

Philadelphia Flyers
A rebuild with real pockets of value, led by volume-shooter Owen Tippett and the Matvei Michkov / Porter Martone ceiling. Martone, in particular, is an appealing target based on his powerhouse 10-game sample at the end of last season. Add Jamie Drysdale, if healthy, as he has a clear path to quarterback the top power play.

Pittsburgh Penguins

The veterans still deliver. Sidney Crosby's a lock until we see otherwise, Erik Karlsson still earns value and Evgeni Malkin remains quietly elite by the minute. Egor Chinakhov is the sleeper pick with deceptive averages from 2025-26, as his half-season Penguins sample (1.88 FPPG) is obscured by his Blue Jackets tenure (0.67 FPPG).

San Jose Sharks

Slated to skate with Macklin Celebrini -- who shares company with MacKinnon, Kucherov, and McDavid's in this year's ultra-elite fantasy quartet -- Will Smith is expected to burst forth with a 70-75 points in his third NHL go-around. Rookie Luca Cagnoni could open many eyes as a super-sleeper by contributing regularly on the top power play. Neither Yaroslav Askarov or Alex Nedeljkovic deserve immediate fantasy attention at the moment.

Seattle Kraken

A fiddle-fit Jared McCann has the potential to reward managers as a late selection in the deepest leagues. Otherwise, Seattle doesn't offer much more than timely streaming options.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

St. Louis Blues

On a top line and power play with Robert Thomas, Jimmy Snuggerud is estimated to shoot up a storm and score near 45 goals in his second full campaign. Aside from the club's top center, Snuggerud boasts the most fantasy appeal up front. The Blues' net now undisputedly belongs to Hofer, while Binnington's future in St. Louis remains uncertain at best.

Tampa Bay Lightning
Elite and safe at the top, with Nikita Kucherov the league's most productive forward minute-for-minute. Watch the power-play battle: John Carlson's arrival threatens Hedman's return to key minutes, and with Victor Hedman now 35 and coming off a ton of missed time, that's the quarterback job to monitor.

Toronto Maple Leafs

The season hinges on a healthy Auston Matthews, with William Nylander the steadier cornerstone alongside him. Rookie Gavin McKenna is the upside name to watch, Darryn Raddysh is a quiet bet to repeat his top-11 fantasy-D finish, and the crease is a timeshare between Anthony Stolarz and Sergei Bobrovsky that deserves a watch, not a draft-day reach.

Utah Mammoth

Dylan Guenther is a legit 40-goal threat, ex-Islander Anders Lee is one to watch as a depth threat in a plum lineup spot, while Clayton Keller is expected to go about his usual business of scoring near 90 points. The busiest goalie in 2025-26, Karel Vejmelka could lose a few more starts to Sebastian Cossa, who's ready to prove himself after four solid seasons in the minors, but not enough to sweat about.

Vancouver Canucks

As frustrated as Canucks fans are with their former star, Elias Pettersson is still worth rostering in fantasy leagues that treasure more than production. No forward blocked more shots this past season and those points add up. Brock Boeser and Jake DeBrusk could be worth a whirl in exceptionally deep fantasy competition. On the blue line, Zeev Buium is worth monitoring.

Vegas Golden Knights

What should fantasy managers make of Carter Hart's potential this year? After a whole year off, the netminder was more than just reliable for a Golden Knights team that made it all the way to the Stanley Cup Final. But he played only 40 games total between the regular and postseason. There are other starting netminders, for other good squads, who carry less uncertainty. Otherwise, Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner rank one and two up front, respectively, while Mark Stone -- the most valuable of the three when healthy -- best suits rosters with plenty of IR spots.

Download the ESPN Fantasy Sports app and have every player right at your fingertips. Available on the App Store and Google Play.

Washington Capitals
New faces Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou reshape a lineup still leaning on Alex Ovechkin's shot volume. It's a huge forward upgrade - and rookie Cole Hutson is a solid gamble, having generated power-play points at the best per-minute rate in the league in a small sample; the Protas brothers add homegrown upside.

Winnipeg Jets

As of this very minute, Stuart Skinner is the clear-cut No. 1 in Winnipeg while Connor Hellebuyck remains on the outs. If that situation holds, the two-time Stanley Cup Finalist could reward his managers handsomely as a third or fourth fantasy goaltender. As for the inactive former Hart/Vezina Trophy-winner, he's bound to be traded at some point (right?) and worth a fantasy gamble in mid rounds of most drafts. A healthy Cole Perfetti is poised to take it to the next level on a top line and power play with Mark Scheifele, who scored a rather quiet 103 points this past year.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: No Cavan? No problem for surging Philadelphia
stories.summary: Philadelphia lost three star youngsters to international duty, yet the Union continued their march toward the top of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

Hany Mukhtar became the 16th player in MLS history to score 100 goals after netting twice in a 2-0 win against Toronto. With seven games to go, Nashville is ten points clear (although Vancouver has a game in hand) as the Music City side seek its first Supporters' Shield.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

STL had the weekend off while it prepares for the Red Bulls on Wednesday.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

Despite a 3-0 win against RSL last weekend, it's been a so-so string of results for the Whitecaps after drawing D.C. 3-3. That's one win in four games across all competitions, although it's still mathematically possible to steal the Shield from Nashville.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Miami (and Lionel Messi, with an incredible free-kick goal, of course) helped close out the weekend with one of the more entertaining games of the matchday. But Miami walked away with a 2-1 loss to Columbus after a 98th-minute winner from the Crew. Santiago Morales getting sent off for time wasting two minutes earlier didn't help.

5. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

In a battle of two teams that are soaring in the second half of their season, Philly came out the victor in a 4-2 win against Orlando. With three players on international duty with the United States (including Cavan Sullivan, the team's second-highest goal contributor), Milan Iloski and Indiana Vassilev balled out, both clocking three goal contributions each with the former netting a hat trick.

6. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 5

After losing 3-0 in Utah, New England's first loss in four games came against a struggling RSL side. With a chunk of the Revolution's starting XI on international duty, including two of their three top goal contributors, it's a stumble but not a nose dive.

7. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 8

Charlotte's 1-0 loss at home to fifth-place Chicago could prove pivotal as we get closer to the playoffs. With the defeat, the fourth-place Crown is just one point ahead of the Fire in the Eastern Conference, and in picking up a late red card, Tim Ream will be absent for Charlotte's next game.

8. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 9

With Houston already trailing, Héctor Herrera's needless red card just before halftime did little to inspire a second-half comeback in a 2-0 defeat to SKC.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 7

With six players on international duty, including both top scorers, LAFC fell 1-0 to Dallas. With one win in ten games, Black and Gold announced they've parted ways with head coach Marc Dos Santos.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 10

Antoine Griezmann was back in the starting lineup against Philadelphia after missing one match and contributed an assist, but it wasn't enough to get back in the win column. After the 4-2 defeat, Orlando has lost two straight games by that same scoreline. It's a shift from its five-game undefeated run, which ended with its U.S. Open Cup loss to Columbus, but it has a chance to make amends, starting with Columbus next weekend.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 11

Chicago's 1-0 win against Charlotte is its first in eight games across all competitions, but it puts the Fire within reach of a top-four spot in the East, as they now trail fourth-place Charlotte by one point. Johan Gómez scored the difference-maker off a corner to mark his first goal tally since returning from the Bundesliga.

12. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

Without key players (including the league's second-highest scorer, Petar Musa) Dallas beat LAFC 1-0 with a roaring header from Osaze Urhoghide off a corner. Ironically, the Black and Gold's late would-be equalizer that was called off for a light foul came from a corner, too.

13. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 12

Dropping points in a 2-2 draw against almost-bottom-of-the-East Atlanta will grate as the Pigeons hover just above the playoff line. As ATL's late equalizer came off a goalkeeping mishap, the absence of Matt Freese (on international duty for the U.S.) was keenly felt.

14. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 17

With a brace from Preston Judd (his fourth goal in three games), San Jose stretched its undefeated streak to six games after a 3-1 win against Portland. Every point counts as the playoffs loom; the Quakes finished the weekend in the West's top four, but two teams trail by just one point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 15

After notching a 3-2 come-from-behind victory against Colorado, the Galaxy have two straight 3-2 wins against teams vying for playoff positions. Those points could matter down the line, as they finish the weekend even with the Rapids, who still sit just above them in the table.

16. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 13

With six players missing for international duty, Cincinnati's defensive troubles continued in a 3-1 defeat to the Eastern Conference's last-placed team, Montréal. Cincy has now conceded 17 goals in its past five games. Success in the final third can only do much when you're that leaky at the back.

17. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

San Diego was sailing toward a 3-0 win until the 73rd minute, when it let Austin launch a late comeback in a 3-3 stalemate. SDFC now have two draws in two games but haven't won since Aug. 29. They could have used the three points: they've got seven games to break into the playoff positions but are three points and three places short of the wild-card spots in a very competitive Western Conference.

18. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 20

After beating Minnesota 3-1, Seattle has two wins in two games (including a midweek victory over RSL) and is undefeated in seven. And if it wasn't for Drake Callender's five saves, they would have scored more. With a game in hand, it finished the weekend just inside wild-card positions out west.

19. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

RSL got their first regular-season win since May 16 in a 3-0 victory over the Revs. As the team looks for answers, 19-year-old Aiden Hezarkhani opened the scoring early to mark his first tallies since March, while Sergi Solans notched a brace to mark his first since mid-August.

20. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 21

Brandon Vázquez scored a late diving header that inspired a three-goal comeback (Christian Ramírez had the others) in a 3-3 draw against San Diego. Not a bad way for Vázquez to score his first of the season.

21. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

RBNY took the weekend off but play again on Wednesday.

22. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 23

After closing out the weekend with a last-minute goal to seal a 2-1 win over Miami, Columbus is on a bit of a roll. The Crew have three wins in three games across all competitions, putting them four points (but still three places) shy of the wild-card spots in the Eastern Conference playoff race.

23. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 22

Paxten Aaronson isn't on Mauricio Pochettino's experimental young USMNT roster this month, but he registered his third goal and fifth goal contribution in four games in a 3-2 loss to the Galaxy. That's a small high note in a loss that could matter in the coming weeks, as the seventh-place Rapids are now even on points with eighth-place LA with seven games to go.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 24

The good news: Callender made some good saves. The bad news: it wasn't enough to stop a five-game losing streak or pick up their first win since Aug. 22.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 25

After losing 2-0 to Nashville, Toronto's commendable form has taken a turn with three straight defeats. The Reds have a more forgiving match against bottom-of-the-east Montréal up next.

26. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

In his eighth game for D.C., 24-year-old Kimito Nono scored twice to mark his first for the team in a 3-3 draw with Vancouver. D.C. is still winless in three games, but that's a respectable result against a top team.

27. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

Atlanta did well without its stars on international duty, absconding with a point against NYCFC in a 2-2 draw. The Five Stripes are still second bottom in the East and six points shy of the playoff spots, but they have just one loss in five games (three draws, one win).

28. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 26

Portland took a trip to NorCal and came away with a 3-1 defeat to the Quakes. That's three straight defeats for a team that's somehow just one spot and three points outside the playoff positions.

29. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Montréal clocked its first regular-season win since Aug. 19 in a 3-1 victory over Cincinnati. After beating Vancouver in the Canadian Championship semifinal, that's two wins in three games for the MLS basement dwellers. Progress?

30. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

SKC beat Houston 2-0 with help from Herrera's red card and two first-half goals, including one strike and assist from André Luiz, marking five goal contributions in the past three games for their big signing.

stories.body:

stories.headline: Lando Norris apologises to Franco Colapinto after calling for ban
stories.summary: Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto after he called for the Alpine driver to be banned following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has apologised to Franco Colapinto after he called for the Alpine driver to be banned following Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Colapinto triggered a three-car pile-up at a safety car restart on lap 36 that took his teammate Pierre Gasly and Norris out of the race.

Speaking to media shortly after the accident, Norris pointed the blame at Colapinto, hinting that the Argentine driver does not deserve to be on the F1 grid.

"If you cause a crash on a restart like this, you should have at least a one-race ban," Norris told media after the race.

"I just got taken out. And the FIA should be stricter by starting to hand out bans for this kind of stuff.

"You want to be against the best drivers and when stuff like this happens it is because, yeah, they shouldn't be there."

In an Instagram post on Monday, Norris said his comments were made in the heat of the moment and revealed he had already apologised directly to Colapinto for what he said.

"Tough weekend overall in Baku and of course a disappointing and early end to the race," Norris wrote.

"After the race, I sent Franco a message apologising for the comments I made that I simply should not have said. I know better and emotions were running high but that is not an excuse, it was wrong of me. I've made mistakes of my own over the years and I know this is very much a part of racing and fighting on the limit.

"Me and Franco came to a good understanding, are still good friends and are both excited to get back racing this weekend."

Colapinto, who was hit with a five-place grid penalty for triggering the accident, apologised to Gasly and Norris immediately after the race.

"Very sad and disappointed," Colapinto said. "Big, big sorry, it's a big mistake. Cold brakes, cold tyres, I was completely out of control. Unfortunately, I also took Pierre out. And Lando of course. Big sorry to both of them."

Norris' original post-race comments provoked a bombardment of online hate toward the British driver across his social media channels -- largely from supporters of Colapinto.

The backlash led Alpine to issue a statement -- the fourth of its kind published by the team this year -- condemning the online abuse.

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

- Azerbaijan Grand Prix: Alpine to consider next steps after Colapinto, Gasly DNF

Ahead of the Baku weekend, Gasly revealed his girlfriend and his family had received online threats after he held up Colapinto in the closing stages of the Madrid Grand Prix.

Colapinto has built a big fanbase in his home country of Argentina since making his F1 debut in 2024.

Colapinto will serve his five-place grid penalty at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix, which will be hosted at Malaysia's Sepang circuit.

stories.headline: NRL tease 11-minute act with GF entertainment back on
stories.summary: The NRL's Grand Final entertainment is back on, with Peter V'landys teasing a mystery 11-minute slot before kick off at Accor Stadium.
stories.body:
The NRL's Grand Final entertainment is back on, with Peter V'landys teasing a mystery 11-minute slot before kick off at Accor Stadium.

Less than a week after it emerged the NRL was without a main act for Sunday's decider, the game's executive chairman confirmed on Monday that had changed.

"I've got to tell you it'll be the highest-rating 11 minutes you will ever see, because no one knows what it is, and we won't tell until the night," V'landys told reporters.

"And a lot of people will be surprised.

"There will be something, but I am not saying what it is. Stay tuned."

The NRL had faced public backlash over the decision to go without pre-match entertainment, after talks broke down with Australian artist Tones and I.

Saturday's headline-grabbing performance by Kylie Minogue at the AFL Grand Final fuelled the criticism.

V'landys had insisted last week it was not an issue that the NRL would go without, comparing the prematch entertainment to a pickle in a burger.

The executive chairman had also pledged to spend $1 million on grassroots rugby league, instead of having that money allocated towards an artist.

Asked on Monday if that money would still go to junior league, V'landys said it would and that a smaller amount was going towards an entertainment act.

"My prime aim was to give $1 million to kids who can't play the game," he said.

"Under-privileged kids, that can't buy boots, that can't get registered, who can't get insurances, who have all their mates playing and they can't.

"That to me is more important than anything. And I want to develop that fund into millions of dollars, not just a million dollars.

"There is something else now that will take some expenditure, but not quite to the level that we would normally spend."

V'landys' comments came as the NRL launched a new initiative on Monday, with fans of Newcastle and the Sydney Roosters marching from opposite ends of the harbour bridge.

Fans of the Broncos were also present, ahead of their NRLW Grand Final against the Roosters.

The NRL is desperate to find new ways to expand Grand Final week, after talk of a third-place playoff and Indigenous All Stars game was largely knocked back by players this season.

Those are still on the table as future options, but a more likely scenario remains turning the NRLW decider into a stand-alone event from as soon as next season.

"We want a festival of rugby league. It's clean air, you have no other product on. You can really promote the game," V'landys said.

"Is it time to have NRLW as stand-alone? Possibly. We may look at them as a Friday night at Allianz Stadium.

"And give them their own window and let them promote themselves. The women's game is a great game and deserves to stand alone.

"At this stage of its evolution it is so far ahead of any other women's sport."

stories.headline: AJ Dybantsa named cover athlete for 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball
stories.summary: The Washington Wizards star began collecting cards this year and will be the cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball.
stories.body:
Fresh off being the top pick of the 2026 NBA draft, AJ Dybantsa was named cover athlete of 2026 Topps Flagship Basketball, the company announced on Monday. Pre orders are set to be available on Oct. 6.

The Washington Wizards rookie never imagined being on a Topps cover, he told ESPN.

"Topps has been in the business for such a long time, putting out cards before I was born," the 19-year-old told ESPN. "So the fact that I'm a cover athlete, I don't take it lightly. I'm very grateful and appreciative for it."

(Image courtesy of Topps)

Dybantsa is the second consecutive top overall pick to be the cover athlete, with Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg getting the honors last year. Flagg and Dybantsa are both from the New England area: Flagg from Newport, Maine, and Dybantsa from Boston.

Their shared region is something the Wizards forward pointed out when reflecting on following Flagg up.

"Us both being from New England, just putting on for our side of the map," he said. "The northeast doesn't get a lot of love, other than tristate, in my opinion. So us both being from New England, trying to put on for the cities, it feels good."

The Topps Flagship Basketball boasts 20 cards per box with 12 cards per pack. The collection is headlined by a strong 2026 draft class. Following Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson went No. 2 to the Utah Jazz, Cameron Boozer went No. 3 to the Memphis Grizzlies and the Chicago Bulls took Caleb Wilson at No. 4.

Autographed cards of rookies, as well as of veterans and legends, are included. There are also new inserts, including a first-ever Gold one-of-one All Kings parallel, according to Fanatics.

And Dybantsa is the face of it, following a year where his interest in collecting cards grew. When he started signing cards, he started collecting, too, and even has two of himself -- one he bought at Fanatics Fest in July and the other he pulled randomly.

Once the Wizards selected him with the top pick in June, Dybantsa walked on stage, shook NBA commissioner Adam Silver's hand and headed to ESPN's set for an interview. By the time he took his seat, his first NBA rookie card was made. Dybantsa then signed it live on air.

"It was crazy. I don't even know how they did it, to be honest," he said. "I just took the picture, walked the stage. I don't know how they got the card that fast, but it was super exciting. ... I hope to get it one day, but someone else might."

Being a Topps cover athlete should presumably give Dybantsa the upper hand on securing the card. It would only be appropriate, especially since his interest in having his own card has intensified.

Attending Fanatics Fest added to that desire.

"You end up going to that little area where they sell all the cards. And then you just have people bidding, people bidding for my card and it's like now I want to get into it," he said. "I want to collect my own card. So the dude was actually able to help me out and get my first signed card."

Dybantsa currently owns probably 100 "important" cards, meaning numbered or signed ones. There are visions for a collectibles room in his house with signed jerseys and "cards would for sure be a part of that," he said.

It wouldn't just be basketball ones, either. He highlighted that he owns one of France and Paris Saint-Germain soccer star Ousmane Dembele. He tries to collect cards of his friends plus former or current teammates.

However, Dybantsa hasn't yet asked which of his Wizards teammates are into collecting.

"I'll figure it out," he said. "Might have to make some trades."

stories.headline: Lynx's Olivia Miles unanimous WNBA Rookie of the Year
stories.summary: Olivia Miles has been named the unanimous WNBA rookie of the year, becoming the sixth player in Lynx history to earn the honor.
stories.body:
Minnesota Lynx star Olivia Miles has been unanimously voted the Kia WNBA Rookie of the Year.

The second overall pick in this year's draft, Miles averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds for a Lynx team that finished with the league's best record at 33-11.

Miles broke Caitlin Clark's record for most points by a rookie and was the only first-year player named to this year's All-Star Game.

Miles' efforts were key for the Lynx as star Napheesa Collier didn't make her season debut until mid-July because of offseason surgery on both ankles.

Miles is among six Minnesota players who have been named Rookie of the Year, a list that includes Crystal Dangerfield (2020), Collier (2019), Maya Moore (2011), Seimone Augusts (2006) and Betty Lennox (2000).

Miles and the Lynx hope this season still has more games left in it. Despite being the No. 1 seed in the playoffs, Minnesota is down 1-0 in its first-round series against the New York Liberty after a 91-75 loss Sunday. Miles scored 11 points and had a team-high eight rebounds in the loss.
