Sorokin was New York's undisputed MVP last season, posting a .906 SV% and 2.68 goals-against average in 55 appearances. He can mask (no pun intended) other issues (such as, ahem, scoring struggles) and give the Islanders a chance to win even when they aren't lighting up the scoresheet. Behind Sorokin is a solid defense anchored by reigning Calder Trophy winner Schaefer. The sophomore will drive New York from the back end with bursts of speed that still surprise opponents. And Schaefer's increasing power-play prowess stands to elevate that unit after it finished 30th last season (at just 16.5%). There's no limit to what Schaefer can offer, and that's the best thing for the Islanders.

Biggest concern: New York doesn't boast an arsenal of scoring threats. The Islanders were 25th in that category last season -- the problematic power play certainly didn't help -- and New York failed to add any needle-movers in the offseason to aid their offensive efforts this season. That leaves Mathew Barzal and Bo Horvat to try to make the Islanders at least competitive up front. It will be harder than ever to do, considering Anders Lee departed in free agency to leave New York with only four players from last season who tallied over 40 points (yikes). On the plus side, Kyle Palmieri is returning from an injury that sidelined him most of last season. But even then, how can the Islanders expect marked improvement? It's a question they've had to answer before -- and never with much success.

This season hinges on ... how Pete DeBoer can leave his mark on the Islanders. New York went off a cliff late last season and cost itself a playoff spot and former coach Patrick Roy his job. DeBoer was brought in with just six games remaining to understand the issues and now he has got to turn things around. The new bench boss already identified areas of concern, including that "stagnant" power play, that must be addressed, but DeBoer also has to work on the team's culture to help guide New York toward better days. Expectations for the Islanders are admittedly low; there are too many holes in the group to suggest New York can rebound from how last season ended. Boosting those spirits with a strong start to the season goes a long way. Does DeBoer have the messaging required to make it happen? That's what New York should be depending on.

Most likely award winner: Pete DeBoer, Jack Adams Award

Fantasy outlook: Rookie Matthew Schaefer is the real deal, an every-week anchor from Day 1 in top-pairing, power-play minutes. He has a real shot at being the top fantasy defenseman already, if the Islanders' underwhelming power play can find its form under coach Peter DeBoer. -- Allen

Bold prediction: Isles become trade deadline sellers. -- Wyshynski

23. Columbus Blue Jackets
Last season: 40-30-12 (92 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +6000

Projected points: 97.4

Biggest strength: The Blue Jackets have a signature star in Zach Werenski. He's not just the NHL's reigning Norris Trophy winner, but Werenski is the backbone of Columbus' best asset, which is a solid defense that can mask some inconsistencies in generating offense. Werenski was not just the Blue Jackets' points leader in 2025-26 (with 81 in 75 games), but he also led the league in shots on goal by a defenseman, paced all blueliners in high-danger shots and proved that the way he uses speed and skill to be a 200-foot phenom sets the tone for his teammates. Columbus gets major output from its back end, with four defenders eclipsing the 30-point mark last season, and the potential is there to have those same contributions in the coming season. That's a win.

Biggest concern: It was a dramatic summer for Columbus that featured several of its high-profile players in the headlines. How the ongoing narratives affect players, and possibly their performance, could be a huge problem. Werenski's rumored unhappiness and trade request -- ahead of him reaching free agency in July 2027 -- was one talking point. Whether to move top forward Kirill Marchenko -- a soon-to-be RFA who doesn't appear committed to the organization -- was another. And GM Don Waddell has been clear that he will not move Marchenko, so that narrative could carry on for a while (Waddell, at least, got Adam Fantilli to sign a new six-year deal). Still, there are substantial internal and external issues to juggle, and Columbus is facing it now without former captain Boone Jenner, who departed for Washington in free agency. Who steps up to be the leader the Blue Jackets need in navigating a pivotal juncture for the organization?

This season hinges on ... how well Columbus responds to coach Rick Bowness. The veteran bench boss took his team to task at the end of last season, saying his group "didn't care" about losing and calling for a "change [to] this freaking culture." It's time now for Bowness to back up his words with action. Given the distractions the Blue Jackets are already facing regarding impending free agents, potential contract holdouts or even sizable trades, it's not ideal to have players on eggshells around the coach. Bowness can't lose the Blue Jackets' dressing room or else the team is in for another disappointing finish.

Most likely award winner: Zach Werenski, Norris Trophy

Fantasy outlook: Zach Werenski is a set-and-forget anchor, and Adam Fantilli is ready to pop in his age-22 season. Valeri Nichushkin is the bounce-back dart -- a proven scorer whose value cratered on availability, not ability -- and Jet Greaves owns a crease that's worth your attention if Columbus banks him wins. -- Allen

Bold prediction: Kirill Marchenko isn't traded. -- Wyshynski

24. St. Louis Blues
Last season: 37-33-12 (86 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +20000

Projected points: 93.8

Biggest strength: This offseason, the Blues attempted to address their scoring challenges from last season. The lack of goals was instrumental in the Blues finishing four points shy of the final Western Conference wild-card spot. How would they adapt after finishing bottom 10 in scoring? They sought to do just that by landing Connor McMichael in the trade that sent Jordan Kyrou to the Capitals, and adding Mason McTavish via trade from the Ducks. McMichael finished last season with 46 points -- the same number as Kyrou -- whereas McTavish, despite his consistency issues, had 17 goals and 41 points.

Biggest concern: Did they really fix the offensive issues? Go back to the start of last season. St. Louis had one of the strongest offseasons because it appeared the Blues were poised to receive contributions from every line. Only to then be one of the worst teams in the NHL in the offensive zone, a detail that was more amplified by being in the bottom 10 in high-danger scoring chances per 60 and scoring chances per 60.

This season hinges on ... how their young core responds to the challenge at hand. St. Louis is banking on Dalibor Dvorsky increasing his production after a 12-goal rookie season, Dylan Holloway scoring 30 goals, Mason McTavish tapping back into the promise that made him a legitimate top-six center in years past, Jake Neighbours having his third 20-goal season in the last four years and Jimmy Snuggerud continuing to build on his 21-goal and 51-point rookie campaign.

Most likely award winner: Jim Montgomery, Jack Adams Award

Fantasy outlook: On a top line and power play with Robert Thomas, Jimmy Snuggerud is estimated to shoot a lot and score near 45 goals in his second full campaign. Aside from the club's top center, Snuggerud boasts the most fantasy appeal up front. -- Matiash

Bold prediction: Dylan Holloway scores 30 goals, 70 points. -- Wyshynski

25. New York Rangers
Last season: 34-39-9 (77 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +8000

Projected points: 93.6

Biggest strength: The Rangers reinvented their roster in the offseason, and it should lead to better results on the ice. The big-swing trade for Pavel Dorofeyev from Vegas gives New York a 25-year-old forward hitting his prime with high-end scoring ability. The Rangers desperately needed an impact player to replace some of what was provided by Artemi Panarin, who was traded to L.A. Having Dorofeyev should boost J.T. Miller and/or Mika Zibanejad to make New York's offense its greatest asset (aside, of course, from netminder Igor Shesterkin, who remains one of the NHL's top netminders). The depth additions of Oliver Bjorkstrand and Eeli Tolvanen up front, plus Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson on the blue line, will also serve New York in being well-rounded. There's an opportunity now for the Rangers to learn from past mistakes and embrace a new way forward.

Biggest concern: New York has got to prove its depth is strong enough down the middle and in net. The Rangers have been burned before by relying too heavily on Shesterkin's elite capabilities, and with a new backup in the fold (Joonas Korpisalo), there could be a tendency to put too heavy a load on Shesterkin early, and that could become a stumbling block by midseason. Perhaps more pressing, though, is that even with an infusion of exciting forwards, New York doesn't have an overflowing crop of centers. Beyond Miller and Zibanejad, there's Joe Veleno (another offseason addition), Noah Laba (fresh from a 24-point rookie season), and ... that's about it. However the pivot position plays out only compounds the pressure on New York's wingers to put up substantial numbers. Again, it ties back to a potentially fresh sort of identity for the Rangers, but without a real roadmap yet of how it will unfold.

This season hinges on ... how well New York puts all the new pieces together. The Rangers' challenge in having options is figuring out who goes where and whether there's immediate chemistry. New York knows from recent experience that a slow start to the season -- especially one that includes a shockingly poor record at home -- can sink a campaign practically before it gets rolling. If coach Mike Sullivan struggles to find new lines that click, or defensive pairs who sync up, the Rangers could be in a difficult spot again by November and face an uphill battle back to the playoffs. The talent, at least, is there for Sullivan & Co. It's a matter of expediting the feeling-out process to have the new and old guard settled in sooner rather than later.

Most likely award winner: Igor Shesterkin, Vezina Trophy

Fantasy outlook: Loaded with established talent at the key positions: Mika Zibanejad, Adam Fox and an elite Igor Shesterkin in net. Alexis Lafreniere is the sleeper worth a late flier, as he found another gear late once the offense reshuffled after Panarin was dealt, finishing in the top 50 in fantasy points after March 1 last season. -- Allen

Bold prediction: Gabe Perreault doubles his goal total from last season (12). -- Wyshynski

26. Nashville Predators
Last season: 38-34-10 (86 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +20000

Projected points: 87.6

Biggest strength: The optimism presented by the members of their new-look supporting cast. Roles are always subject to change throughout the season, but the Predators landed a top-nine center in Mavrik Bourque. They also strengthened their middle- and bottom-six forward group with Ross Colton, Jack Drury, Nils Hoglander and Alexander Kerfoot. They could also get significant contributions from 2025 first-round pick Brady Martin, 2022 first-round pick Reid Schaefer and Vitali Pinchuk, who signed a one-year contract after averaging more than a point per game in the KHL last season.

Biggest concern: Any team that comes within a close margin of a playoff spot is forced to look at what caused it to fall short. Their losing streaks hindered the Predators throughout the season. The Predators had four losing streaks of more than three games before December. Two of them included skids of four or more games. They had three more extended losing streaks later in the season -- and then missed the playoffs by just four points. Keep in mind, six of those losses were decided in overtime.

This season hinges on ... attaining consistency and stability in a few areas; an example is offensive metrics. The Predators were tied for the 10th-best power play and ranked 11th in high-danger chances per 60. Although they were around league average in scoring chances per 60, they were 20th in goals per game. It was similar to their defensive structure. They were either at or slightly above league average in allowing the fewest high-danger and scoring chances per 60, yet were in the top four in most shots allowed per 60. And if that's not enough, Nashville was around the league average in team save percentage in 5-on-5 play but allowed the seventh-most goals per game.

Most likely award winner: Brady Martin, Calder Trophy

Fantasy outlook: Making a sparkling impression in preseason competition, Matthew Wood is worth monitoring. On the blue line, perhaps because of Nashville's underwhelming showing and recent injuries, Roman Josi isn't garnering the fantasy attention of previous seasons. If healthy, the 2020 Norris winner remains a fringe top-10 defender. -- Matiash

Bold prediction: Matthew Wood breaks out. -- Wyshynski

27. Detroit Red Wings
Last season: 41-31-10 (92 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +15000

Projected points: 79.7

Biggest strength: The Red Wings should feel good about their marquee players -- namely, Moritz Seider, Alex DeBrincat and Lucas Raymond. At 25, Seider is hitting his prime as a dominant threat at both ends of the ice. (Plus, he can handle huge minutes, such as last season's 25:40 per game.) DeBrincat eclipsed the 40-goal mark in 2025-26 and was a key to Detroit's excellent power play, which ranked 12th in the league, and he projects to be again. Raymond continues to expand his repertoire as a strong two-way forward who consistently punches in 20-plus goals per season. That's a young, strong, smart group capable of stacking up with some of the NHL's best performers.

Biggest concern: Detroit has holes deeper in the lineup and an apparent gap in leadership. Dylan Larkin's (still-unfulfilled) trade request stripped him of the Red Wings' captaincy, and Detroit replaced former GM Steve Yzerman with a temporary manager in Shawn Horcoff. That's an unsettling turnover with the potential to throw the team off course. There are other pain points to address, too. Defenseman Simon Edvinsson is an RFA without a new deal. Patrick Kane and David Perron aren't around to boost Detroit's depth and offer some veteran presence. And a shortened training camp won't help this team forge new bonds and find its rhythm with a dressing room that could feel understandably off-kilter. Then, there's the question of goaltending -- can John Gibson still be a top netminder in the league? And how well will Daniil Tarasov fare in his first season backing up for the Red Wings? The unknowns have added up in the Motor City.

This season hinges on ... how Detroit manages Larkin. One player probably won't make or break Detroit's season (even an elite-level forward such as Larkin). But there is bound to be some trickle-down effect from the team's options here. The real issues come with: a) keeping a disgruntled skater and risking him going from a top center to a potential liability, or b) honoring Larkin's trade request but without getting a player in return to backfill his contributions. Both would be real issues. Keeping an unhappy Larkin could lead to a crumbling of Detroit's dressing room dynamic. How comfortable will players be with him -- and each other -- moving forward? Chemistry is foundational for every top team, and if Todd McLellan is expected to get the Red Wings back to the playoffs (after they've been missing out for the past decade), they have to play as a group.

Most likely award winner: Alex DeBrincat, Art Ross Trophy

Fantasy outlook: Moritz Seider anchors an elite peripheral profile, but the forward core carries questions after Patrick Kane's departure and Dylan Larkin's ugly offseason. Fade Alex DeBrincat: He was fourth in the league in shots per minute last season, but that chemistry with Kane is off the table now. -- Allen

Bold prediction: Dylan Larkin stays in Detroit. -- Wyshynski

28. Winnipeg Jets
Last season: 35-35-12 (82 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +15000

Projected points: 77.7

Biggest strength: Winnipeg still has an experienced foundation with Kyle Connor, Dylan DeMelo, Adam Lowry, Josh Morrissey, Neal Pionk, Mark Scheifele and Gabriel Vilardi. The Jets could also use this season to gain a firmer grasp on where things stand with their youth movement. Brad Lambert, Isak Rosen and Brayden Yager are all first-round picks who could take on larger roles this season, and the same could be true for 2026 first-round pick Viggo Bjorck.

Biggest concern: Connor Hellebuyck and his desire to leave Winnipeg. The Jets suspended their star goalie after he declined to attend training camp. Hellebuyck, a three-time Vezina Trophy winner who also won the Hart Trophy in 2025, has remained an integral part of Winnipeg's foundation. Winnipeg has a fallback plan in place. The Jets signed Stuart Skinner, a proven starter who is on his third team in the past year, and could also rely on Thomas Milic, who has three games of NHL experience.

This season hinges on ... how the Jets manage their multifront challenges: the Hellebuyck situation, trying to cultivate the young players and their need for some new scoring solutions. Connor, Scheifele and Vilardi combined to score 46% of the Jets' goals in 2025-26 -- a statistic that underscores their need to find new answers in 2026-27.

Most likely award winner: Kyle Connor, Rocket Richard

Fantasy outlook: As of now, Stuart Skinner is the clear-cut No. 1 in Winnipeg while Connor Hellebuyck remains on the outs. If that situation holds, Skinner could reward his managers as a third or fourth fantasy goaltender. Hellebuyck is bound to be traded at some point (right?) and worth a fantasy gamble in the middle rounds of most drafts. -- Matiash

Bold prediction: Scott Arniel is fired. -- Wyshynski

29. Chicago Blackhawks
Last season: 29-39-14 (72 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +25000

Projected points: 77

Biggest strength: Their continued commitment to surrounding their young core, led by Connor Bedard, Artyom Levshunov and Frank Nazar, with more veterans. The Blackhawks did that this offseason, ahead of what could be an important campaign with Bedard entering his first season as captain. They have added multiple Stanley Cup winners -- such as Bowen Byram and Ian Cole -- along with Patrick Kane, one of the all-time greatest players in franchise history who won three titles with the Blackhawks. Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi will serve as alternate captains, alongside Bedard, as the young core continues to develop.

Biggest concern: Having a repeat of their 2025-26 season would raise questions, considering the challenges the Blackhawks faced then (including extended absences from Bedard and Nazar). Overall, they were in the bottom two in allowing the most high-danger scoring chances per 60 minutes, scoring chances per 60 and shots per 60. Scoring also wasn't easy. The Blackhawks averaged the second-fewest goals per game last season, as part of a composite in which they finished in the bottom two in shots per 60, scoring chances per 60 and high-danger scoring chances per 60.

This season hinges on ... building continuity. The Blackhawks will need to improve their overall performance, as evidenced by their underlying metrics, which should allow them to take the next step. Last season, they finished with 72 points, which was an 11-point improvement over the previous season. Reaching the 80-point mark for the first time since the 2018-19 season appears to be in play if they're not one of the worst teams in the league in either the defensive or offensive zone.

Most likely award winner: Connor Bedard, Art Ross

Fantasy outlook: Patrick Kane and Roman Kantserov (fresh from the KHL) are set to pile up points while flanking Connor Bedard at even-strength and with the extra skater, once the star center returns from injury. No one will be shocked to see Kane hit the 70-point mark in his return to Chicago. No. 1 option on Chicago's blue line, Bowen Byram could rank as a top-20 defenseman once all is said and done. -- Matiash

Bold prediction: Anton Frondell is a top-three rookie scorer. -- Wyshynski

30. Seattle Kraken
Last season: 34-37-11 (79 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +40000

Projected points: 70.5

Biggest strength: What goaltenders Joey Daccord and Philipp Grubauer did last season was important for a few reasons. Only the Avalanche finished last season with a better team save percentage in 5-on-5 play. But their performances also provided consistency for a team that has struggled in that department. Of course, the Kraken having a .917 save percentage in 5-on-5 play raises questions about why their overall team save percentage was .902.

Biggest concern: Only the Canucks, who finished with the worst record in the NHL, had a poorer penalty kill than the Kraken last season. The Kraken had a 72.2% success rate whenever they were defending the extra-skater advantage. The defensive struggles extended into what they did at 5-on-5. Having the fifth-lowest shot share in the NHL meant they spent more time defending than attacking. That was further compounded by the fact that they were in the bottom 10 in allowing the most high-danger chances per 60 and shots per 60 in 5-on-5 play.

This season hinges on ... if they can show significant improvement across the board in nearly every aspect. Yes, there are the defensive issues. But the same applies to their offensive zone efforts. They were last in high-danger chances per 60 and scoring chances per 60, and were in the bottom 10 in shots per 60. Put it all together, and the Kraken were in the bottom 10 in goals per game and goals allowed per game.

Most likely award winner: Joey Daccord, Vezina Trophy

Fantasy outlook: A healthy Jared McCann has the potential to reward managers as a late selection in the deepest leagues. Otherwise, Seattle doesn't offer much more than timely streaming options. -- Matiash

Bold prediction: Kraken win the 2027 draft lottery. -- Wyshynski

31. Calgary Flames
Last season: 34-39-9 (77 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +100000

Projected points: 67

Biggest strength: The acknowledgement of their collective situation. The Flames know that they are in a rebuild. They know they have young players who are at different stages. Players such as Matt Coronato, Dustin Wolf and Connor Zary are further along than Matvei Gridin, Samuel Honzek and Zayne Parekh, but all must continue to be developed properly. There's also the addition of Simon Nemec, and what he can provide now that he has a much clearer lane to operate as a top-pairing defenseman after the logjam with the Devils.

Biggest concern: There are several items that are concerning for the rebuilding Flames. Calgary's defensive structure was among the most porous in the NHL last season, in the top 10 of allowing the most high-danger chances per 60, scoring chances per 60 and shots per 60. The offensive structure also encountered similar struggles, as the unit was in the bottom 10 of those same categories when in the offensive zone.

This season hinges on ... something foundational being done to help for the future. So what does that entail? It starts with the front office gaining a firmer grasp on the young players who will use 2026-27 to further develop their identities. There's also how the front office manages the trade deadline, and the draft capital the team attains. And as is customary for any rebuild, it is imperative to be in the strongest possible position for the draft lottery.

Most likely award winner: Dustin Wolf, Vezina Trophy

Fantasy outlook: A key player of the Flames' future, Zayne Parekh could make significant fantasy noise in anchoring the top power play. A must-roster in dynasty competition, the 20-year-old defenseman is also worth targeting in deeper redraft leagues. -- Matiash

Bold prediction: Matvei Gridin becomes a "must-watch" player. -- Wyshynski

32. Vancouver Canucks
Last season: 25-49-8 (58 points), missed playoffs

Stanley Cup odds: +100000

Projected points: 53.9

Biggest strength: Clarity about their situation. Think about the roller coaster that has been -- and possibly always will be -- the Canucks, especially over the past few years. They've gone from being a win away from going to the Western Conference finals in 2023-24 to missing out on the playoffs by six points in 2024-25 to finishing last in the NHL by more than 10 points in the 2025-26 season. The reality about their current and future situation was further compounded by other changes, ranging from trading franchise player and captain Quinn Hughes to making sweeping changes in their front office and behind the bench.

Biggest concern: When a team finishes with the worst record in the NHL, this likely means everything is a concern. Defense is a concern. Why? Because the Canucks allowed the most goals per game, were in the bottom three in allowing the most high-danger chances per 60, scoring chances per 60 and shots per 60. They also had the worst penalty kill. The Canucks were also in the bottom three in goals per game while being in the bottom 10 in generating high-danger chances per 60, scoring chances per 60 and shots per 60.

This season hinges on ... how the next several months can help build a foundation for the future. Rebuilds are largely powered by either getting the first pick or a high draft selection. Another is attaining as much draft capital as possible. Vancouver has five players entering the final year of their contracts. It's possible the Canucks could move on from some of those players in their bid to add more picks to a haul that already has 10 draft selections in 2027, and 28 in total over the next three years.

Most likely award winner: Filip Chytil, Masterton Trophy

Fantasy outlook: As frustrated as Canucks fans are with their former star, Elias Pettersson is still worth rostering in fantasy leagues that treasure more than production. No forward blocked more shots last season, and those points add up. Brock Boeser and Jake DeBrusk could be worth a whirl in exceptionally deep fantasy competition. -- Matiash

Bold prediction: Marco Rossi becomes a No. 1 center. -- Wyshynski

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 39
Goals: 35
Assists: 15

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami

Messi, 39, will play his final match in his national team's jersey when Argentina take on Benin in an Oct. 6 friendly at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium, following his announcement in late August that he was ending his international career. But before heading to Argentina, he gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

International breaks this season

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

stories.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.

George Russell closed the gap in the drivers' championship to 66 points from his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli after taking his third win of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Antonelli, who was hampered with all sorts of issues across the weekend, recovered from P16 to finish fifth.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the next race.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- George Russell warns 'pressure' is on Kimi Antonelli after 'most dominant weekend in my career'

- Lando Norris: Drivers should have 'one-race ban' after collision with Franco Colapinto at Azerbaijan GP

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 2

Practice One: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Saturday, October 3

Final Practice: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Sunday, October 4

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: 8 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the Bahrain GP being hosted in Malaysia?
The Bahrain Grand Prix was cancelled in April due to the war in Iran, but it has now been rescheduled and will now be staged in Malaysia, meaning the race will remain on the F1 calendar.

There were several reasons why Malaysia was an obvious alternative, the main one being the way the calendar fell and the logistics involved.

It sits between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took place at the weekend, and will be followed by the Singapore Grand Prix on Oct. 11, resulting in a triple-header.

The last time the Malaysia Grand Prix held a race was in 2017. It spent 18 years on the calendar, so the infrastructure is there to be able to host a race with not much notice.

Sepang International Circuit

The Sepang is one of the circuits that is a complete test of car performance and driver ability. There is a mixture of long straights, heavy-braking zones and fast, flowing corners.

It is always one of the most humid races and due to the tropical weather, there can be heavy downpours of rain, changing the course of a race in an instant.

The combination of weather and the characteristics of the circuit always provide an exciting race and it is a driver and fan favourite as a result.

There is a tight hairpin at Turn 15, but either side are long straights which provide excellent overtaking opportunities.

Previous winners in Malaysia

2010: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2011: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2012: Fernando Alonso (Ferrari)

2013: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1999

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Lap record: 1:34.080 Sebastian Vettel (2017).

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel with four victories (2010-2011, 2013 and 2015). From the current grid, Fernando Alonso with three (2005, 2007 and 2012), Lewis Hamilton (2014), and Max Verstappen (2017) have each won here.

Most poles: Michael Schumacher (1999, 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2004) and Lewis Hamilton with five (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017). From the current grid, Alonso has two poles (2003, 2005).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is thundery showers and light winds through the weekend with highs of 33°C.

What happened in 2017?
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in dominant fashion after qualifying third on the grid. It was Lewis Hamilton's race to lose after he put his Mercedes on pole for the race which he's won once before, but he crossed the line in second.

Verstappen's teammate Daniel Ricciardo finished third, while Sebastian Vettel, who started from the back of the grid after suffering engine problems at Ferrari, managed to recover positions on the grid to finish fourth overall.

Vettel was 34 points behind Hamilton in the drivers' championship with five races to go.

Who will win this year?

There will be a slight element of the unknown heading into Malaysia given that over half of the grid have never raced here before. Teams and drivers have historic data to go off, but nobody will really know how the cars will perform until Friday's practice.

Russell didn't put a foot wrong last time out at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was incredibly quick all weekend and will carry that momentum into the next round.

Mercedes are also due to bring a major upgrade to Malaysia, while McLaren are expected to be strong around the high-speed circuit.

Red Bull brought major upgrades to Baku and were well in the fight, so rival teams will be keeping a close eye on Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

With rain expected, and it being one of the most popular circuits in F1, it could be an absolute thriller.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.
